title: Bring Your Own Schema: How We Built kniv v7
gist: Dragonscale released kniv v7, six Apache-2.0 encoder models (55M-538M parameters) that extract user-defined entities, relations and fact attributes locally without LLM calls. On matched document-level relation extraction it beats GPT-6 by 26 F1 points and runs about 90x faster on a laptop CPU, with the author crediting label variety, positive-unlabelled training and calibration over architecture.

themes.theme: Local encoders vs hosted LLM extraction

insights.claim: Dragonscale positions kniv v7 as resolving the trade-off between LLM extraction (flexible but one API call per message) and local taggers (cheap but fixed to trained labels), arguing agent memory needs LLM flexibility at tagger cost.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Signals a wedge for small open encoders to displace per-call LLM spend in agent-memory pipelines.
insights.quote: Agent memory needs the first one's flexibility at the second one's cost.
insights.locator: An LLM can extract anything

insights.claim: On a matched comparison on the full Re-DocRED test set with gold entities supplied, kniv v7 scored 0.733 F1 on document-level relations versus 0.477 for GPT-6, a 26-point lead.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Specialist small models can decisively beat frontier LLMs on structured extraction tasks.
insights.quote: Document-level relations: kniv is 26 points ahead.
insights.locator: Coreference: level.

insights.claim: Even when GPT-6 was explicitly handed every candidate entity pair, at 5.4 times the number of calls, it reached only 0.545 F1 on Re-DocRED relations.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Throwing more LLM calls at structured extraction raises cost sharply without closing the gap.
insights.quote: Even handed every candidate entity pair explicitly, at 5.4 times the calls, GPT-6 reached only 0.545.
insights.locator: Document-level relations: kniv is 26 points ahead

insights.claim: The author attributes GPT-6's relation-extraction weakness to pair selection: 75% of its misses were pairs it never proposed and 81% of its false facts were on pairs holding no relation.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Identifies a concrete structural failure mode of LLMs that architecture-specific models exploit.
insights.quote: 75% of GPT-6's misses were pairs it never proposed, and 81% of its false facts were on pairs that hold no relation.
insights.locator: The relation gap has a clear cause

insights.claim: On reported scores, kniv v7 beat GPT-6 on every linguistic task (e.g., LAS 0.929 vs 0.885, NER 0.870 vs 0.849), and the author observes that the more structural the task, the bigger the specialist's lead, though GPT-6 linguistic scores were on 300-item samples rather than matched runs.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Suggests a rule of thumb: the more structured the output, the more defensible a specialist-model business.
insights.quote: the more structural the task, the bigger the specialist's lead
insights.locator: On the reported scores, the more structural

insights.claim: On 60 LongMemEval messages with a 30-relation, 15-entity-type schema, GPT-6 via hosted API took a median 31.4 seconds and about 1,820 input and 2,248 output tokens per message, versus 0.35 seconds for kniv UltraBERT INT8 on an M2 Max laptop CPU with no billed tokens.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Roughly 90x latency advantage plus zero marginal API cost undercuts hosted-LLM unit economics for high-volume extraction.
insights.quote: kniv's median is about 90 times faster than the hosted call, on a laptop CPU, with no per-message API fees and nothing leaving the machine.
insights.locator: On this workload, kniv's median

insights.claim: Running extraction locally means no data leaves the machine, which the author frames alongside speed and cost as an advantage over hosted LLM extraction.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Privacy-preserving on-device inference is a selling point for regulated or personal-memory use cases.
insights.locator: On this workload, kniv's median

themes.theme: Open-schema design and data over architecture

insights.claim: kniv v7 lets users define entity types and relations in plain English at run time, with no training or labelled examples, and returns facts annotated with polarity, modality, holder and time.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Run-time schemas make one model reusable across CRM, support, codebase and memory verticals.
insights.quote: Change the relations list and you've changed what the model looks for. No training and no labelled examples are needed.
insights.locator: Change the relations list

insights.claim: The prior v6 model reached 0.764 F1 on Re-DocRED but only for that benchmark's fixed 96 relations and 6 entity types, which the author calls useless for support desks, CRMs, codebases or personal memory.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Benchmark-optimized fixed-schema models have limited commercial value; flexibility is the product.
insights.quote: For a support desk, a CRM, a codebase or a personal memory, it was useless.
insights.locator: Our previous research line (v6)

insights.claim: Transplanting the fixed relation head into a label-reading head never regained parity (0.755 vs 0.764) and scored only 0.204 on unseen 8-way FewRel relations.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Architectural retrofits alone do not deliver zero-shot generalization.
insights.quote: The architecture could read labels. It just hadn't learned to.
insights.locator: The first attempt was surgery

insights.claim: Pretraining on thousands of knowledge-base relations, each worded multiple ways, lifted unseen FewRel accuracy from 0.204 to 0.480, more than any architectural change tried; the author concludes label variety beats architecture.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Data diversity, not model design, is the moat in zero-shot extraction.
insights.quote: label variety beats architecture
insights.locator: The finding that changed the plan

insights.claim: The team found its own teacher-annotated data, however large, narrowed zero-shot behaviour to its own labelling style.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Scaling proprietary synthetic labels can reduce generalization, a caution for LLM-distillation data strategies.
insights.quote: Our own teacher-annotated data, however large, narrowed zero-shot behaviour to our own labelling style.
insights.locator: The finding that changed the plan

insights.claim: A frozen encoder with adapters capped relation F1 at about 0.76, so v7 pretrains the encoder itself for knowledge first and then trains every head on it.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Representation quality, not add-on heads, limits extraction performance.
insights.locator: The second finding was that the encoder

insights.claim: Experiments that changed supervision moved results while those changing heads mostly did not: a learned entity linker did not beat exact name matching plus coreference, and bigger typing heads moved CrossNER under a point while costing 3 points on Few-NERD.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Reinforces that data pipelines are where value accrues in applied NLP.
insights.quote: the limit was usually the data, not the head.
insights.locator: The lesson that runs through

insights.claim: LLM teacher labels measured against gold were precise but incomplete, at 0.71 precision and 0.31 recall, so naive training would turn two-thirds of true facts into negatives; v7 therefore trains positive-unlabelled throughout.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Shows LLM-generated training data is materially incomplete and needs specific handling.
insights.quote: They were precise but incomplete: 0.71 precision, 0.31 recall with gold entities.
insights.locator: Much of our relation supervision

insights.claim: Each training stage ran on a single A100 40GB in bf16, indicating the model family was built on modest compute.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Competitive specialist models can be built cheaply, lowering barriers for small labs.
insights.quote: Each stage ran on a single A100 40GB in bf16.
insights.locator: Each stage ran on a single

themes.theme: Calibration as a cheap performance lever

insights.claim: Early zero-shot thresholded F1 was 0 even though the correct relation was usually top-ranked; one offset chosen on held-out data fixed it, so calibration.json now ships with the weights.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Large quality gains can come from post-hoc calibration rather than retraining.
insights.quote: The model knew the answer. Its scores were just on the wrong scale for an unseen relation to clear the threshold.
insights.locator: The most surprising number

insights.claim: Moving the entity-span offset from 0 to about -2 was worth up to 8 points per CrossNER domain with no retraining.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Run-time tunability lets customers adapt models to new domains without ML spend.
insights.locator: The span offset is the clearest case

insights.claim: On Re-DocRED, even thresholds tuned on the test set add at most 1 point; the gold relation ranks first for 72-73% of facts and in the top four for 98%, so remaining errors are in pair selection and ranking.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Defines the ceiling of calibration and where further R&D must focus.
insights.quote: So what remains is choosing pairs and ranking, not thresholds.
insights.locator: Calibration also told us

insights.claim: With thresholds chosen on dev, the tiny student's end-to-end Re-DocRED score rose from 0.38 to 0.54 without retraining.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Small models especially depend on calibration to be usable.
insights.locator: Calibration matters even more for students

insights.claim: kniv v7 is a family of six Apache-2.0 models from 55M to 538M parameters (built on Ettin, ModernBERT, DeBERTa-v3-large and UltraBERT-380M), all with the same call and outputs.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Permissively licensed, size-tiered open models broaden deployment from edge devices to servers.
insights.locator: So today we're releasing kniv v7

insights.claim: In a pre-registered bake-off, no single encoder won: DeBERTa-v3-large led linguistic and fixed-schema tasks, UltraBERT-380M led zero-shot knowledge tasks by 4.2 points and handles longer windows, and Ettin-400M was dropped.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Encoder choice is task-dependent; no one backbone dominates.
insights.quote: No single encoder won.
insights.locator: We ran a bake-off

insights.claim: Mixing the two teachers' outputs per task beat either teacher on every head (+2.2 SRL, +2.7 relations, 1.3-2.2 on entity types), and students learn that mixture, including rankings and label vectors.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Ensemble distillation is a practical way to get cheap models that exceed any single source.
insights.locator: Two teachers are better than one

insights.claim: Every scored student beats both teachers at 5-way FewRel and the large model leads at 15-way; the author guesses learning the mixture's rankings over thousands of relation names generalises better, but has not tested why.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Smaller distilled models can outperform larger teachers on generalization, favoring cheap deployment.
insights.quote: Every student we've scored beats both teachers at 5-way FewRel, and large leads at 15-way.
insights.locator: The students are better at zero-shot

insights.claim: The author recommends kniv-v7-large-en (221M, ModernBERT-base) as the default: within a point of the better teacher on tagging, parsing, NER and SRL and within two on document relations, at about twice the speed.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Mid-size models hit the price-performance sweet spot for production.
insights.quote: large is the one to start with.
insights.locator: large is the one to start with

insights.claim: Distilling one teacher's relations into the other failed: UltraBERT gained 0.35 on Re-DocRED but lost 2 to 3 zero-shot points, so the author advises running both models and averaging for best relations (+2.7 F1).
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Best quality still requires ensembling, a compute trade-off for buyers.
insights.quote: If you need the best relations, run both models and average them.
insights.locator: Distilling one model's relations

insights.claim: Students trained only on hard labels, where 1.7% of facts are negated, never predicted negation (F1 0.00 for smallest); distilling attribute predictions and oversampling negated windows brought large to 0.72.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Rare-class behaviors are easily lost in distillation, a hidden quality risk.
insights.locator: Attributes have to be distilled too

insights.claim: Tripling small-student training to 30,000 steps improved relations (tiny +4.7 Re-DocRED, +6.8 on 10-way FewRel) but not NER, SRL or coreference, which are limited by encoder capacity; below about 70M parameters coreference is the clearest cost.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Clarifies which capabilities scale with training versus parameter count.
insights.quote: Below about 70M parameters, coreference is the clearest cost of the smaller size.
insights.locator: Coreference is where size shows most

insights.claim: Plain INT8 quantization collapsed UltraBERT's Re-DocRED score from 0.754 to 0.168 because massive activations (about 8,000 vs typical ~4 in layer 14) consumed the per-tensor scale.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Naive quantization can silently destroy model quality; deployment engineering is a real moat.
insights.quote: Plain INT8 destroyed UltraBERT: Re-DocRED went from 0.754 to 0.168.
insights.locator: Plain INT8 destroyed UltraBERT

insights.claim: SmoothQuant fixed INT8: UltraBERT INT8 held relations at 0.747 vs 0.754 fp32 while cutting CPU time per 200 words from 1.07s to 0.47s and the encoder graph from 1.6 GB to 0.53 GB.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Roughly 2x speed and 3x size reduction with negligible loss makes CPU-only deployment viable.
insights.locator: SmoothQuant fixed INT8

insights.claim: The models run via ONNX with only onnxruntime, tokenizers and numpy, with no PyTorch needed, and the tiny model runs 200 words in 0.09s on an M2 Max CPU in INT8.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Minimal dependencies and sub-100ms latency enable embedding in edge and consumer devices.
insights.locator: Each repository ships ONNX graphs

insights.claim: Agreement with fp32 is the wrong quantization check: INT8 changes about 15% of semantic-role arguments but costs only 0.2 points against gold, so the INT8 gate now scores against gold.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Evaluation methodology choices can mislead about deployment risk.
insights.quote: Agreement with fp32 is the wrong check.
insights.locator: Agreement with fp32 is the wrong check

insights.claim: kniv v7 trails specialist competitors on zero-shot relation classification (RE-Matching 0.926/0.829 vs ~0.73/0.675 at 5/10-way) and on CrossNER (GLiNER-large 0.613 vs 0.580), but is well ahead of GLiNER on Few-NERD (0.523 vs 0.317).
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Maps the competitive landscape of open extraction models where kniv leads and lags.
insights.quote: Where we trail: zero-shot relation classification against RE-Matching, and CrossNER against GLiNER-large.
insights.locator: Where we trail

insights.claim: End-to-end Re-DocRED relations reached 0.627 with an open schema, beating the fixed-schema v6 at 0.566, while the open schema costs about 3 points with gold entities.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Flexibility no longer costs end-to-end accuracy, strengthening the open-schema product case.
insights.locator: End-to-end relations beat our fixed-schema v6

insights.claim: On a LongMemEval memory probe of 150 questions with a generic schema, the answer appeared in UltraBERT's extracted entities for 0.69 of questions and in facts for 0.48, with temporal and multi-session questions weakest.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Shows local extraction alone is not yet sufficient for full agent memory recall.
insights.locator: Memory. We ran a memory probe

insights.claim: Known limits include about 29% of gold document facts missed, near-synonym relation confusion, no cross-window linking, imperfect conversation attribution, unreliable negation and reported speech, and English-only support.
insights.speaker: Rohit Rai
insights.so_what: Buyers must budget for downstream memory and verification layers.
insights.quote: Treat polarity and modality as signals to check, not guarantees.
insights.locator: Where It Breaks
